column3: Spaced-repetition system (SRS) flash card program
column10: The BEST flash card/SRS platform around. You can study pre-built decks like Kaishi 1.5k, or build your own decks (e.g. with Rikaitan!).  If you are beginner, start with a beginner vocab deck! If you are intermediate but find your vocab lacking, it is worthwhile downloading a vocab deck, then browsing the cards and "suspending" all of the vocab you already know by heart (or just relearn them for practice.) If you are more upper intermediate, it is recommended to mine your own vocab from native content, but you may find some prebuilt decks useful.
column11:
How to Use Anki ・ Kaishi 1.5k Basic Vocab Deck・ Beginner's Vocab from Anime Deck
   Anki is free on desktop and Android (AnkiDroid), but for a free iOS app you may have to hunt around. The official app on iOS is paid, but you can also access your decks and do reviews from Safari by going to ankiweb.net.
It may be easier to search for prebuilt decks via Google/Reddit/etc. than it is to use Ankiweb's built-in search.

column3: Comprehensive dictionary; pre-generated vocab decks for books/anime; SRS platform
column10: More thorough than most dictionaries in that it compiles lots of info about every word or kanji. Includes kanji decompositions, example sentences, examples words that use a particular kanji, example kanji that use a kanji, frequency info, ...
column11:
See for example: 解読-Vocab and 解-Kanji. You can even search for an anime and see full vocab lists for each episode, e.g. here! About jpdb's SRS platform - it could kind of be an Anki alternative, if you really don't want to use Anki. it automatically teaches you dependencies of a word before that word, including kanji components. For example, before teaching you 読解, you will learn 言,売,読; and 角,刀,牛,解. (It gets much more granular than that actually). Also, it tracks what you know across decks, which is super neat!
There are decks for Genki and Minna no Nihongo if you happen to be learning using one of those!
